extracted.intended_audience: anyone who communicates on behalf of an organization responding to major emergencies (e.g., public health communicators, emergency managers, organizational spokespeople)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations and communicators on planning, crafting, and delivering messages during crises and emergencies, including audience tailoring, spokesperson roles, community engagement, and media relations. Emphasizes evidence-based practices across phases of a crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based framework and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The CERC manual provides an evidence-based framework and recommended practices for anyone who communicates on behalf of an organization responding to major emergencies such as natural disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CERC's evidence-based framework and recommended practices as the foundation for organizational crisis communication efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core CERC principles and phase-specific application
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication principles and how they apply to each phase of a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply foundational CERC principles (as described in the Introduction) to planning, response, and recovery phases; adapt tactics according to the crisis phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how people process information during a crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes how people process information differently during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize altered information processing in crises when designing messages (e.g., simplified messages, repetition, prioritizing key actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and address psychological barriers to receiving information
rubrics_metrics.description: Psychological barriers to receiving information, and how to incorporate what we know into strategies for communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate barriers (fear, denial, overload) and incorporate strategies to overcome them into message design and delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider audiences' needs when crafting messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Different ways to consider your audiences' needs, and the factors that can influence their understanding and acceptance of your messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience characteristics, needs, and concerns; design messages that match their literacy, cultural context, and informational priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor messages for different audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: How communicators can tailor their messages for different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audiences and adapt content, tone, channel, and calls to action to increase comprehension and acceptance among each group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community identification and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: How to identify and engage with communities who are affected by crises and promote active community participation in responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map affected communities, engage stakeholders early, foster two-way communication, and promote community participation and trust-building activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement a crisis communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How to develop and implement a crisis communication plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create actionable plans that define roles, messages, channels, procedures, and triggers for activation; test and revise plans regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson role and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of a spokesperson in communicating during crises and emergencies and recommendations on practices for spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define spokesperson selection criteria, messaging responsibilities, media training, consistent messaging, and best practices for public appearances and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with the media and fostering positive media relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The media's role in a crisis and recommended practices for facilitating positive relationships with the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish proactive media relations, provide timely and transparent information, coordinate messaging, and support journalists' information needs to improve coverage and public understanding.
